QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_25

question.text: Nari Shakti Trust has formed 200 Self-Help Groups (SHGs) in Odisha; 120 women have started micro-enterprises. A state government scheme is also active in the same area, training SHG members and subsidising micro-credit. Under SAS-400, how should the SIA handle the assessment of the Trust's contribution?

answer.text: Claim 100% of enterprise formation as Nari Shakti's attributable impact
Drop the indicator since attribution is impossible
Compare results with the baseline or benchmark and what would have happened in the absence of the project, and disclose contribution and deadweight assumptions to avoid overclaiming
Treat the entire change as the government scheme's effect and assign zero credit to the Trust

explanation.text: The Logic: Workbook guidance is to assess what would have happened in the absence of the project or activity, examine how much could have happened irrespective of the intervention, and use deadweight to avoid overclaiming the SE's contribution. Comparing observed results against a baseline or benchmark and against the absence-of-project scenario, while disclosing contribution and deadweight assumptions, is the supported approach. The Trap: Option A overclaims; Option B gives up on assessment when a defensible comparison is possible; Option D swings to the other extreme and ignores the Trust's role. Note: Document the baseline or benchmark used, the assumed absence-of-project scenario, and the deadweight basis directly in the working papers so the contribution claim is auditable.
